affectedPublicSurfaces: THE `inventory_items` IDENTITY ITSELF. `models.py::InventoryItem` (line 265) declares `quantity`, a NULLABLE `warehouse_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100))`, `velocity`, and pins one row per SKU per shop with `Index("ix_inventory_shop_sku", "shop_id", "tiktok_sku_id", unique=True)`. This slice widens that identity to `(shop_id, tiktok_sku_id, warehouse_id)` and adds `committed_quantity`. A two-warehouse SKU is not representable today, which is why ADR-093 d.2's warehouse-allocation guard has nothing to validate against.

THE WAREHOUSE DISCRIMINATOR BECOMES **NOT NULL**, AND THAT IS THE HAZARD THE ISSUE RECORDS. Postgres treats NULLs as DISTINCT inside a unique index, so a three-column unique over a nullable `warehouse_id` would readmit exactly the duplicates it is meant to forbid — the index would look total and enforce nothing. The migration must therefore backfill a documented single-warehouse SENTINEL into every NULL `warehouse_id` FIRST, then `SET NOT NULL`, then build the new unique, then drop the old one. Two further properties of the sentinel are load-bearing and must be stated in the PR: (a) it must be a value TikTok can never return — captured warehouse ids are long numeric strings (`7272949914115966726`, `contract-collection.md` A-8), so an empty string, `"0"` or a numeric-looking value is NOT safe; (b) once RI-2 (#1795) starts emitting the SKU's REAL warehouse id, a row that was backfilled to the sentinel will not be updated in place — the upsert will insert a SECOND row and leave the sentinel row behind as a stale orphan carrying the pre-widening quantity. Decide deliberately whether RI-1 or RI-2 owns retiring those rows, and say which in the PR; discovering it in production is the failure this bullet exists to prevent.

`committed_quantity` ARRIVES AS A COLUMN THAT NOTHING WRITES YET. `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so every existing row stays valid and the previous release — which names the column nowhere — keeps inserting through `InventoryRepo` unchanged. Grep proves the starting point: `committed_quantity` has ZERO hits anywhere under `backend/src` today. The vendor returns it (`total_committed_quantity` at SKU level and `committed_quantity` per `warehouse_inventory[]` entry, both visible in capture A-8), `expand_inventory_search` never reads it, `_transform_inventory` never maps it — those three layers are #1795's, not this slice's.

`suppliers` — A NEW TABLE, ONE STABLE RECORD PER SHOP PER SUPPLIER: name, lead time in days, contact fields (email, phone, messaging handle) and a supplier-SKU → Juli-SKU ALIAS MAP THAT STARTS EMPTY and fills as receipts are confirmed. This replaces ADR-093 d.2's payload-level "supplier and lead time remembered from the seller's prior runs", which has no store at all today — the scope verification found the only homes for such facts are free-form JSON (`ActionCard.recommendation_payload`, `WorkflowRun.state`) and the demo's hardcoded prose (`apps/demo/src/lib/workflows/replenish-inventory/plan.ts:62`). The empty alias map is the join a v2 document source needs on its first line (global research §2, §3).

`purchase_orders` — A NEW TABLE WITH A CHECK-CONSTRAINED STATE MACHINE: `draft → sent → acknowledged → partially_received → received → closed`, with the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OUTCOME (`as_is | with_changes | rejected`) AS ITS OWN COLUMN, not folded into the state. That triple is EDI 855's and Odoo's, and in v1 a human sets it after reading a chat message (global research §2, §4). Carries supplier reference, subject SKU, order reference, quantity ordered, expected date and needed-by date. An illegal transition must fail closed with a NAMED error and leave the row's state untouched.

`receipts` — A NEW TABLE, ONE ROW **PER DELIVERY**, with `accepted` and `short` per line. There must be NO aggregate `qty_received` column on `purchase_orders` carrying the same fact: retrofitting multi-shipment onto a `qty_received` column is the documented trap (`research/supplier-connectivity-global-tools.md` §2 — "Receipt is a separate entity, not a PO field", Shopify's transfer, Zoho's Purchase Receive, Odoo's backorder). The absence of that column is an assertion against the live Postgres catalog, not a code-review opinion.

`supply_events` — A NEW TABLE, THE INTAKE PIPE'S LEDGER (ADR-093 amendment 2026-09-08 (a)): `source` (v1 accepts `seller_form` ONLY), the parsed fields, a **per-field** confidence (not one document-level score — Rossum's and Zoho's pattern, global research §4), a source-document reference where one exists, and `confirmed_by` / `confirmed_at` which stay NULL until a human confirms. This shape is what makes a later photo, e-invoice or Excel source an additive row rather than a re-design; none of those sources exist at any version in this slice.

TENANCY CLASSIFICATION IS PART OF THE PUBLIC SURFACE, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. `inventory_items` is already `tenant_direct` in `database/tenant_scoped_tables.py`, so the identity widening adds no policy there. But `suppliers`, `purchase_orders`, `receipts` and `supply_events` are FOUR NEW TABLES that hold tenant data and must each be classified in `TABLE_CLASSIFICATION_MAP` (`tenant_direct` where they carry `shop_id`, `tenant_via_parent` where they hang off a parent) AND given their RLS policy and grants in the same revision. The map's own docstring makes this fail-closed: "an unclassified table FAILS the proof", consumed by the isolation proof (#1329) and the boot-time precondition check (`workers/agent_runtime_boot.py`, #1330). W7's migration 045 already shipped once with two tenant-scoped tables missed and #1329's proof is what caught it; do not repeat that here.

NO HTTP SURFACE CHANGES AND NO RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. No route, no seller-visible string, no repository method asked for a new column, no reader of the four new tables — they stay EMPTY until RI-4 (#1800) writes the first supply event. This slice must be a read no-op for the running process. If implementation finds itself editing a service, a route or a mapper to make a test pass, the scope has slipped: the sync is #1795, the signal #1798, the write #1802.

migrationCompatibility.notes: THIS IS THE ONE REAL SCHEMA SLICE OF W10-C. Four ADDITIVE tables (`suppliers`, `purchase_orders`, `receipts`, `supply_events`) that no code reads and no code writes until RI-4, plus `inventory_items.committed_quantity` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` — a default the previous release satisfies without naming the column. The one non-additive step is the identity widening, and it is EXPAND-THEN-CONTRACT in a strict order inside a single revision: (1) backfill the documented single-warehouse SENTINEL into every NULL `warehouse_id`; (2) `SET NOT NULL` on `warehouse_id`; (3) CREATE the three-column unique on `(shop_id, tiktok_sku_id, warehouse_id)` — legal while the stricter two-column unique still stands; (4) DROP `ix_inventory_shop_sku`. Never the reverse order, and never step 3 before step 1: with NULLs still present the new index is not total, because Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. No column is renamed, retyped or dropped and no data is destroyed. The previous release keeps working with every one of these present: it writes `warehouse_id` sometimes NULL — which is why the NOT NULL is the one coexistence edge to state in the PR, with the chosen remedy (a server default of the sentinel, or holding the NOT NULL until #1795 always supplies a warehouse) named explicitly rather than discovered. The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue — NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. W6, W7-bis (#1469), W8, W9 and the sibling W10 lanes all hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries a duplicate-numbered `043_*` pair (`043_stop_reason_consent_pause.py` and `043_juli_app_role.py`, chained one after the other) from exactly that mistake.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: inventory stays one row per SKU per shop, a two-warehouse SKU stays unrepresentable, `committed_quantity` stays dropped at every layer, and no supplier, purchase-order, receipt or supply-event record exists anywhere — the pre-existing state the scope verification recorded, and the exact blockage RI-NFR-1 names. No new exposure, nothing partially applied, no stock touched on any shop.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the PREVIOUS RELEASE FIRST and restart juli-api and juli-celery-worker: it reads and writes none of the new columns or tables, so it runs correctly with them present and needs no downgrade — the one edge is that it may attempt an inventory insert with a NULL `warehouse_id`, which the chosen NOT NULL remedy (server default of the sentinel, or deferring the NOT NULL) must absorb; that remedy is asserted pre-merge, not assumed. Only if the schema must ALSO be reverted, `alembic downgrade -1`, and that downgrade MUST FAIL LOUDLY with a named error, never silently drop data, in three cases: (a) any `receipts` row exists — dropping the table would destroy confirmed-consent evidence; (b) any second-warehouse row exists for one `(shop, sku)` — restoring the two-column `ix_inventory_shop_sku` would be impossible or would require deleting a row; (c) any `supply_events` row is confirmed. All three refusals are asserted pre-merge. Order matters: previous code first, downgrade second, so no live process is mid-write against a column being narrowed.

doNotInfer: Do NOT infer a TikTok replenishment-recommendation endpoint — none exists. The scope verification checked `docs/integrations/tiktok_corpora/partner-catalog.json` and found only packaging (`Get Recommended Product Package`) and title/description/category recommenders. No column, comment or docstring in this slice may describe a stored value as TikTok's recommendation.

Do NOT label a Juli-computed number as TikTok's. Any baseline is computed by Juli with TikTok's dashboard formula and labelled as such (S-NFR-4's no-false-attribution rule). This slice computes nothing, so no such label belongs in it at all.

Do NOT model the stock write as an absolute set anywhere in this schema. The write is a DELTA applied to a freshly re-read level (ADR-093 amendment 2026-09-05); a column named or documented as a target stock level would encode the wrong contract for RI-5.

Do NOT add an uplift column, a multiplier, or any field that presumes an uplift without a seller-entered event date. There is no campaign calendar anywhere — `models.py::Campaign` (line 1090) is a creator-collaboration outcome record with `predicted_gmv`/`realized_gmv`, not a sale calendar — and the uplift applies only to a seller-entered date (§8.3 decision 5).

Do NOT encode an order beyond 90 days of supply as representable-and-flagged. The 90-days-of-supply upper guard suppresses the proposal entirely with a named reason; it is #1798's rule, not a column here.

Do NOT add a supplier API client, a portal, an EDI adapter or a messaging channel of any kind, and do NOT add a Zalo channel. No per-supplier API is in scope at ANY version (ADR-093 amendment (e); none of the eighteen surveyed tools exposes one), and Zalo Notification Service is customer-only by Zalo's own template rules — it is not a supplier channel.

Do NOT treat a supplier message as a confirmed fact. `supply_events.confirmed_by`/`confirmed_at` stay NULL until a human confirms; a parse is a proposal, a confirmation is the consent (ADR-093 amendment (a)). A default of confirmed, or a confidence threshold that auto-confirms, breaks that.
Do NOT hash model-supplied values for a report. The params hash binds the CONFIRMED values the seller saw — that binding is #1800's, and nothing in this schema may presuppose a model-argument hash.
Do NOT create any path that could write stock below the committed quantity. `committed_quantity` exists here so RI-5's invariant is enforceable; this slice adds no writer, and must add none.

The migration number and `down_revision` are RESERVED BY META and supplied with the issue. NEVER run `alembic heads`, never read the tip of `backend/src/juli_backend/database/migrations/versions/`, never derive the number from the newest filename. W6, W7-bis, W8, W9 and the sibling W10 lanes hold unlanded numbers off-tree, and this tree already carries a duplicate `043_*` pair from exactly that mistake.

Do NOT make the warehouse discriminator nullable and call the three-column unique done. Postgres treats NULLs as distinct; the index would enforce nothing while appearing total. The sentinel backfill and the NOT NULL come first.

Do NOT pick a sentinel a vendor could return. Captured TikTok warehouse ids are long numeric strings (`7272949914115966726`); an empty string, `"0"`, or any numeric-looking value can collide with a real warehouse and silently merge two warehouses into one row.

Do NOT add an aggregate `qty_received` (or equivalently named) column to `purchase_orders`. A receipt is a separate entity, one row per delivery — retrofitting multi-shipment onto a single received-quantity column is the documented trap (global research §2).

Do NOT accept a `source` other than `seller_form` on `supply_events` in v1, and do NOT build a photo/OCR, e-invoice, Excel or messaging source. Those are v2 in evidence order (ADR-093 amendment (e)) and are epic deferrals.

Do NOT change the sync, the mapper, the transformer or `InventoryRepo`'s lookup key. The sync keeping every warehouse and carrying the committed bucket is #1795; the signal is #1798; the tool is #1802. This slice is schema only and adds NO reader of the new columns.

Do NOT leave a new table out of `database/tenant_scoped_tables.py::TABLE_CLASSIFICATION_MAP` or without its RLS policy and grants in the same revision. The map fails closed by design — an unclassified table fails the isolation proof — and W7's migration 045 already shipped once having missed two tenant-scoped tables.
Do NOT open the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051); do NOT touch apps/**, packages/** or ios/** — this epic's doNotLoad list.

Bind every test to the REAL model classes and a REAL async session against a real Postgres 16. A fake repository or a `**kwargs` double proves routing, never that the constraint, the index or the CHECK would actually hold.
